dimensions.assessment: Affects holders of federal rights-of-way, easements, or permits on public land, as well as states, political subdivisions, Indian Tribes, and public entities engaging in aquifer recharge.
dimensions.evidence: acting for the holder or on behalf of a State, political subdivision of a State, Indian Tribe, or public entity

dimensions.assessment: Exempts qualifying non-profit aquifer recharge transport uses from additional BLM rent and federal permitting hurdles, while explicitly prohibiting new construction, expansion, or waiver of environmental laws like the Endangered Species Act.
dimensions.evidence: shall be exempt from the payment of additional rent to the Bureau of Land Management

dimensions.assessment: Exempts certain users from additional rental payments to the Bureau of Land Management, but does not provide specific fiscal totals.
dimensions.evidence: shall be exempt from the payment of additional rent to the Bureau of Land Management

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Aquifer Recharge Flexibility Act regarding statutory interpretations, notice requirements, and exemptions for specific right-of-way uses.
dimensions.evidence: The holder of the right-of-way, easement, permit, or other authorization shall submit to the Bureau of Land Management notice of the intended use

dimensions.assessment: Provides an ongoing statutory clarification and exemption framework for eligible right-of-way holders.
dimensions.evidence: use of an existing right-of-way, easement, permit, or other authorization for the purpose of aquifer recharge

missing_information: Quantitative estimates of lost rental revenue to the Bureau of Land Management
Number of right-of-way holders expected to utilize the exemption
importance_detail.rationale: Clarifies rules under the Aquifer Recharge Flexibility Act allowing existing rights-of-way and easements on public lands to be used for aquifer recharge transport without additional Secretarial authorization or rent, under certain conditions and notice requirements.
